issues.description: Removal of outer Delimited() in AlterTableStatementSegment may break valid multi-operation ALTER TABLE statements
issues.detail: The PR changes AlterTableStatementSegment from `Delimited(OneOf(...))` to just `OneOf(...)`, eliminating support for any comma-separated list of alter operations at the top level. While the PR claims the removed test case was 'invalid', TSQL does permit certain comma-separated alter specifications (e.g., the existing pattern that the removed test demonstrated parsed before this PR). The new design only supports multiple operations of the *same* kind (e.g., multiple DROP COLUMNs via inner Delimited). Any existing user SQL relying on mixed comma-separated alterations will silently fail to parse after this change. Confirm whether real-world TSQL ever mixes operations and document the limitation if intentional.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT grammar makes the CONSTRAINT keyword optional in a way that may accept invalid SQL
issues.detail: In the new DROP block (lines ~4790-4800), the inner Delimited wraps `Sequence(Sequence('CONSTRAINT', IfExistsGrammar, optional=True), ObjectReferenceSegment)`. Because the whole `CONSTRAINT ...` inner Sequence is marked optional, the grammar may accept `ALTER TABLE foo DROP bar, baz` without any CONSTRAINT keyword, which is not valid TSQL. The keyword should likely be required on each delimited item, or the optionality scoped differently so that the first item permits omission while still requiring the keyword on subsequent items (matching the MS Learn syntax).

issues.description: IdentityGrammar now permits a negative increment as well as a negative seed
issues.detail: The change adds `Ref('SignedSegmentGrammar', optional=True)` before BOTH numeric literals in IDENTITY(seed, increment). The PR description only mentions 'negative numbers' for the seed. While TSQL does technically permit a negative increment, this is an undocumented expansion in the PR and there is no test fixture covering IDENTITY(1, -1) or IDENTITY(-1, -1). Add a test case or split the change so the intent is auditable.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE NumericLiteralSegment branch has no test coverage
issues.detail: The CreateLoginStatementSegment now accepts NumericLiteralSegment for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE (an LCID like 1033), but the fixture only tests the naked identifier form (us_english). Add a test case such as `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033` so the new branch is exercised. Otherwise a future refactor could silently break the numeric path.

issues.description: Inconsistent identifier types for DEFAULT_DATABASE vs other login object references
issues.detail: DEFAULT_DATABASE now accepts NakedIdentifierSegment, but realistic database names may be bracket-quoted (e.g. `[my db]`). Consider also accepting Ref('SingleIdentifierGrammar') or Ref('ObjectReferenceSegment') to cover bracketed identifiers. Same concern applies to DEFAULT_LANGUAGE for languages with reserved-name-like aliases.

issues.description: No fixture coverage for N-prefixed PASSWORD combined with MUST_CHANGE and option list
issues.detail: The PASSWORD now accepts QuotedLiteralSegmentOptWithN, but the only added fixture is `PASSWORD = N'$trongPassw0rd'` with no MUST_CHANGE and no trailing _option_list_2. Add a test that combines `PASSWORD = N'...' MUST_CHANGE, CHECK_EXPIRATION=ON, CHECK_POLICY=ON` to ensure the full grammar still composes.

issues.description: Table index in DECLARE table variable lacks coverage for multi-column and named-vs-unnamed index variants
issues.detail: The new test in declare_table_type.sql covers only `index idx (id)`. The existing pre-PR test in the same file already covers `index _name (name)` inline on a column. Add an explicit test for a standalone multi-column index `INDEX idx_multi (a, b)` and for a UNIQUE/CLUSTERED variant if TableIndexSegment supports them, to ensure the new placement plays well with TableIndexSegment's full grammar.

issues.description: Removed fixture deletes coverage rather than relocating it
issues.detail: The removed ALTER TABLE statement (`ALTER TABLE dbo.doc_exc ADD column_b VARCHAR(20) NULL CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c`) used to assert that ADD + DROP could be combined in one statement. If the intent is that this is now intentionally unsupported, add a negative-test or a comment explaining why TSQL does not allow it. Silently dropping a test reduces the audit trail.

issues.description: Trailing semicolon missing on new DECLARE test statement
issues.detail: The new DECLARE fixture in declare_table_type.sql omits the trailing semicolon (`)` with no `;`). While TSQL is lenient and the parser accepts it, every other statement in this file ends with `;`. For consistency and to avoid masking statement-terminator edge cases, add the semicolon.

dissents.topic: Whether removing outer Delimited() in AlterTableStatementSegment is a regression or a correctness fix

positions.position: TSQL does not permit mixing heterogeneous alter specifications (e.g., ADD column then DROP column) in one ALTER TABLE per MS Learn syntax. Removing the outer Delimited is a correctness fix and the deleted fixture was indeed invalid SQL that the parser had been over-accepting.

Even if the SQL is technically not Microsoft-recommended, real-world codebases ship it and SQL Server may accept it in some versions. Removing parser support without a deprecation path is a regression for users who linted previously-parsing files.

dissents.topic: Scope of IdentityGrammar negative sign change

positions.position: PR scope says 'negative identity seed' (singular). Only the seed position should accept SignedSegmentGrammar; touching increment expands scope and lacks a test.

TSQL allows IDENTITY(seed, increment) where both are signed integers (per MS Learn, increment can be negative for descending identities). Symmetric handling is more correct and there's no reason to artificially restrict the increment.

dissents.topic: Whether QuotedLiteralSegmentOptWithN is the right abstraction for PASSWORD

positions.position: Reusing the existing QuotedLiteralSegmentOptWithN segment is the right call — it handles both regular and N-prefixed literals uniformly, matches TSQL's permissive string literal rules, and avoids defining a new OneOf branch.

PASSWORDs are not general-purpose Unicode strings; allowing arbitrary OptWithN may invite false positives (e.g., a unicode-prefixed empty string). A narrower OneOf(QuotedLiteral, NQuotedLiteral) with explicit branches would be more auditable.

review.summary: This PR usefully expands TSQL parser coverage for table-variable indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative IDENTITY seed, and delimited DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT lists, with corresponding fixtures. The main concern is the restructure of AlterTableStatementSegment that removes the outer Delimited() wrapper: this is plausibly a correctness fix per TSQL semantics, but it silently drops support for previously-parsing multi-operation ALTER TABLE statements and the deleted fixture is not replaced with a negative-test or comment explaining the intent. Secondary concerns are the DROP CONSTRAINT inner grammar marking the CONSTRAINT keyword optional (potentially over-accepting), undocumented expansion to a negative IDENTITY increment without a test, and missing fixture coverage for the NumericLiteralSegment branch of DEFAULT_LANGUAGE and the N-prefix PASSWORD + MUST_CHANGE combination. None of the issues are clear merge-blockers given the test fixtures pass, but the AlterTable restructure and DROP CONSTRAINT optionality deserve a closer look before landing.
